transcripts.text: Operative report procedure right pterional craniotomy for clipping of right middle cerebral artery bifurcation surgeon of record Dr Williams the patient was placed under general anesthesia and positioned supinely with the head secured in three-point Mayfield rotated 30° to the left neuronavigation was registered and confirmed using craniofacial fiducial points a curved linear incision was made 1 cm anterior to the tragus extending superiorly behind the hairline along the superior temporal line the scalp flap was reflected anteriorly preserving the frontalis branch of the facial nerve via interfascial dissection of the temporalis fascia a single burr hole was placed at the McCarty keyhole using craniotome the dura was separated from the bone with a Penfield dissector a free bone flap was elevated and set aside epidural tack-up sutures were placed the dura was opened in a curvilinear fashion based on the sphenoid wing the microscope was brought into the field and the cilium fissure was identified and sharply dissected in an arachnoid plane allowing separation of the frontal and temporal lobes the right middle cerebral artery bifurcation was identified and the aneurysm neck was dissected a 7 mm titanium clip was applied across the neck complete obliteration was confirmed with micro Doppler and indocyanine green video angiography parent vessel patency was preserved hemostasis was achieved with a bipolar and Surgicel the dura was closed in a watertight fashion using foreign Nurolon interrupted sutures the bone flap was secured with titanium plates and screws the temporalis muscle and fascia were approximated with interrupted three-oh Vicryl skin was closed with a running three-oh nylon suture no complications the patient was extubated and transferred to the neurosurgical intensive care unit in stable condition
